title: Tenant-tempered benchmark + customer onramp protocol for dedicated throughput attestation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a reproducible, tenant-aware load harness and acceptance protocol to certify Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees for new and existing customers. This ticket scopes the benchmark design, harness plumbing, autoscaler-in-the-loop experiments, and a customer-facing onramp test script. Goal: provide a deterministic path (operator + customer checklist) that attests to committed throughput (qps / tokens/sec) with explicit tail-latency targets and guardrails for autoscale oscillation and cross-tenant interference.
acceptance_criteria: A stable harness repository with composable workload profiles (chat-short, doc-gen-long, mixed-tenant) and deterministic seed control
Benchmark runs produce reproducible artifacts: run manifest, raw telemetry, post-processed summary (p50/p95/p99, throughput, error-rate, OOM count, batch-efficiency)
Autoscaler-in-the-loop experiments validate policy knobs: target_utilization, cooldown, min/max replicas, with documented safe ranges for tenant-mixed traffic
Customer onramp script and checklist (canary steps, 24h sustain, rollback triggers) published in Confluence and linked from the console onboarding flow
Signoff checklist for Solutions/SE and SRE with explicit acceptance gates for SLA-attestation and remediation steps
test_plan: Harness architecture: controller (k8s job + operator), generators (multi-process load drivers), ingesters (request replay and synthetic templates), and telemetry pipelines (prometheus exporter -> clickhouse/temporal snapshot)

Workload profiles: define three canonical profiles — convo-short (mean tokens 30, bursty qps), document-gen (mean tokens 1k, steady token-rate), mixed-tenant (50/30/20 tenant split with different SLAs)
Ramp strategy: microburst (10s spike), ramp-to-steady (15m ramp), sustain (24h steady-state), and ramp-down; each run annotated in run manifest

Metrics to collect: per-tenant qps, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, tail-latency drift, error rates, GPU util, GPU memory headroom, KV cache hit-rate, average batch size, autoscaler decision logs and cooldowns
Autoscaler experiments: run sets with varying target_utilization [65, 75, 85], cooldowns [30s, 120s, 600s], and min_replicas constraints to observe oscillation and overshoot behavior
Failure injection: network latency dimmer, simulated OOM on a replica, and temporary capacity loss to validate fallbacks and circuit-breaker behavior
Reproducibility: each run stores a git-sha, harness commit, config blob, seed for random workload generator, and input sample set so runs can be replayed deterministically
Artifacts: run-manifest.json, raw-prometheus.tar.gz, post-processed-csv, latency-distro histograms, and a short human-readable summary for customer signoff
decisions: Use the new bench-runner service (bench-runner v2) instead of k6 for multi-tenant sequencing because bench-runner supports pre-warmed KV cache replay and model-specific tokenization hooks
Telemetry will be exported to an isolated ClickHouse dataset for throughput-cert runs to avoid polluting prod dashboards
Acceptance gates will bias toward tail-latency and error-rate rather than average latency to protect customer experience
Autoscaler will be tested 'in-the-loop' rather than mocked to surface real-world control dynamics; longer cooldowns preferred for heavy long-turn workloads
open_questions: What minimum isolation (node-pinning / tenant affinity) must we promise for P1 customers prior to full fleet QoS?
Do we need legal-reviewed language for the customer-facing onramp doc about potential transient capacity impacts during canary runs?
Can Solutions Engineering run customer pilots with synthetic data in all regions or restrict to US/EU initially?
